'''''Crocosmia'' × ''crocosmiiflora''''', or '''montbretia''', is a garden hybrid of ''[[Crocosmia aurea|C. aurea]]'' and ''[[Crocosmia pottsii|C. pottsii]]'',{{efn|Some sources mistakenly call this a hybrid of ''[[Crocosmia]]'' and ''[[Tritonia (plant)|Tritonia]]''; the basionym of ''C. aurea'' is "''Tritonia aurea''".}} first bred in 1880 in France by [[Victor Lemoine]].<ref name="Parnell 12">{{cite book |last1=Parnell |first1=John |last2=Curtis |first2=Tom |date=2012 |title=Webb's An Irish Flora |publisher=Cork University Press |isbn=978-185918-4783}}</ref> The [[basionym]] of the hybrid is ''Montbretia crocosmiiflora'' Lemoine.<ref name="Nelson">{{cite journal |last=Nelson |first=E. C. |url=http://archive.bsbi.org.uk/Wats19p265.pdf |title=Who was the author of Montbretia crocosmiiflora? |journal=[[Watsonia (journal)|Watsonia]] |volume=19 |pages=265–267 |date=1993}}</ref> In 1932 it was reclassified as ''C.'' × ''crocosmiiflora'' (Lemoine) <small>[[N. E. Brown|N.E.Br.]]</small>,<ref name="Nelson" /> but the common name "montbretia" is still often found in horticultural literature,<ref name=NIEG>{{cite book |editor-last=Everett |editor-first=Thomas H. |entry=Montbretia |title=New Illustrated Encyclopedia of Gardening |publisher=Greystone Press |location=New York |date=1960 |volume=7 |pages=1181–1182}}</ref> and is commonly used in the British Isles for orange-flowered cultivars that have naturalised, while "crocosmia" is reserved for less aggressive red-flowered cultivars.

==Description==
''Crocosmia'' × ''crocosmiiflora'' grows to 90 cm (36 in.) high, with long sword-shaped leaves, shorter than the flowering stem and arising from the plant base, ribbed and up to 20mm wide.<ref name="Parnell 12" /> The base is a [[corm]], a swollen underground stem lasting one year. The flowers are up to 5 cm long and coloured deep orange.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Clapham |first1=A. R. |last2=Tutin |first2=T. G. |last3=Warburg |first3=E. F. |date=1968 |title=Excursion Flora of the British Isles |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=0-521-04656-4}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
In the United States, ''Crocosmia'' × ''crocosmiiflora'' is considered suitable for planting in hardiness zones 5–9, but in more northerly locations it can be planted in the spring and the corms dug out in the fall. The corms should be planted in a well-drained garden soil in full sun to partial shade.<ref name=NIEG /><ref>{{cite book |title=Planting Instructions |publisher=Garden State Bulb Company |location=Vineland, New Jersey |date=2017}}</ref> The hybrid will set viable seed that can be grown as soon as ripe, but as a hybrid it will not breed true to colour.<ref name=NIEG /> In [[Belfast]], [[Northern Ireland]], it is recorded as well-established in a wide range of locations.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Beesley |first1=Stanley W. |last2=Wilde |first2=John |date=1997 |title=Urban Flora of Belfast |publisher=The Institute of Irish Studies, The Queen's University of Belfast |isbn=0-85389 695X}}</ref>

There are over 150 named cultivars within ''C.'' × ''crocosmiiflora'' including:
* 'Babylon'<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/117804/Crocosmia-x-crocosmiiflora-Babylon/Details |title=''Crocosmia'' × ''crocosmiiflora'' 'Babylon' |website=RHS |access-date=22 August 2024}}</ref> − orange-red with yellow throats
* 'George Davison'<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/56402/crocosmia-crocosmiiflora-george-davison-davison/details |title=''Crocosmia'' × ''crocosmiiflora'' 'George Davison' Davison |website=RHS |access-date=22 August 2024}}</ref> − yellow
* 'His Majesty' − flowers large, orange
* 'Jackanapes'<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/70622/crocosmia-crocosmiiflora-jackanapes/details |title=''Crocosmia'' × ''crocosmiiflora'' 'Jackanapes' |website=RHS |access-date=22 August 2024}}</ref> − flowers orange-red, inner lobes golden yellow
* 'Meteor' − orange yellow
* 'Solfatare' − yellow flowers with bronze foliage
* 'Star of the East' {{smallcaps|agm}}<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/118014/crocosmia-crocosmiiflora-star-of-the-east/details |title=''Crocosmia'' × ''crocosmiiflora'' 'Star of the East' |website=RHS |access-date=22 August 2024}}</ref> − light orange with pale centres

Those marked {{smallcaps|agm}} possessed the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]] in 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf |title=AGM Plants April 2023 © RHS – Ornamental |website=RHS |page=30 |date=April 2023 |access-date=21 August 2024}}</ref>

==Invasive species==
''Crocosmia'' × ''crocosmiiflora'' is deemed an [[invasive species|invasive plant]] in the [[United Kingdom]] and the [[Isle of Man]]; also in [[New Zealand]], where it is common on roadsides in the northern parts of the [[West Coast Region|West Coast]] of the South Island. The New Zealand [[Department of Conservation (New Zealand)|Department of Conservation]] classes it as an environmental weed.<ref>{{cite book |last=Howell |first=Clayson |title=Consolidated List of Environmental Weeds in New Zealand |publisher=Department of Conservation |location=Wellington |date=May 2008 |series=DRDS292 |url=https://www.doc.govt.nz/upload/documents/science-and-technical/drds292.pdf |isbn=978-0-478-14413-0 |access-date=22 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090530024209/http://www.doc.govt.nz/upload/documents/science-and-technical/drds292.pdf |archive-date=2009-05-30 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The California Invasive Plants Council (Cal-IPC) lists ''Crocosmia'' × ''crocosmiiflora'' as an [[List of invasive plant species in California|invasive plant in California]], with limited concern and distribution.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cal-ipc.org/plants/paf/crocosmia-x-crocosmiiflora-plant-assessment-form/ |title=Plant Assessment Form: Crocosmia x crocosmiiflora |website=CAL-IPC |date=2017}}</ref>

It is widely naturalised in England and Scotland, especially along the western seaboard from Cornwall north all the way to Sutherland.
